## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. The create
client takes its project from a single value set once at construction
(`AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:271-327`),
and the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` —
aborting the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project
(`applier.py:217-258`, `_cross_project_targets`, added by bug `626d`). With a mapping that lists
several projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration
that guard exists to catch.

## Approach

Two changes, both narrow.

**Create targets the ticket's project.** The outbound create path resolves the destination through
`resolve_project` from the mapping module rather than from the client's single construction-time
value. A ticket that resolves to "not synced" produces no create mutation at all.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares
each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the
mapping's project set. This is deliberately the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays
fail-closed and still aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a
project the store does not sync is caught exactly as it is today. Only keys the store legitimately
owns now pass. Creates remain exempt for the existing reason — their `key` is a local-id placeholder,
not a real key, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` does not match them.

This is the only existing safety property the epic loosens, which is why it is its own story with a
paired test rather than folded into another change.

**Module size.** Two files here are close to the repository's hard 800-line gate, and they are
treated differently on purpose. `dispatch_one.py` is at 796 lines, so the sibling size-relief story
that extracts its `update_one` sub-tree is a prerequisite of this one — four lines of headroom cannot
absorb the create-path change. `applier.py` is at 772 and is deliberately **not** split. A structural
seam exists there (`_apply_batch` and its helpers), but taking it would relocate `_load_acli` and
`_load_concurrency` out of the module against which roughly 62 `patch.object(applier, ...)` test sites
are written — and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move, so those tests would keep
passing while silently exercising the real Jira and git paths instead of their fakes. Against that,
the change needed here is roughly five lines inside `_cross_project_targets` (`:232-257`), which fits
comfortably in the 28 lines available. Splitting `applier.py` for this change would be the mechanical
split the module-size policy forbids; if it ever must be split, the honest first move is the 67-line
`__all__` and the ~126 lines of banner prose in `:1-198`, which disturb no call graph at all.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed
production-shaped mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project
carried on the call is the contract under test.

- Happy path: a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A` and `B` produces a
  create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A`.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises
  `CrossProjectTargetError`. The negative half is what proves the relaxation did not disable the
  guard.
- Precondition assertion: the guard is shown to run **pre-flight** — the fake transport records zero
  writes when the out-of-set mutation raises, proving no partial leak.
- Edge: a ticket resolving to "not synced" produces no outbound mutation of any kind.
- Collateral invariant: with a single-project mapping the guard behaves exactly as before — an
  out-of-project key raises, an in-project key passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An outbound create targets the ticket's own resolved project rather than the client default;
      checked by a fake transport asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [ ] An update inside the configured set proceeds and one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [ ] A ticket resolving to not-synced emits no outbound mutation; checked by asserting an empty
      mutation list for it while a synced sibling produces one.
- [ ] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
